reply.emotion: excited and triumphant, celebrating a victory
notes: gewinnen takes the auxiliary verb haben in the perfect tense: hat gewonnen.
Do not confuse gewinnen (to win) with verdienen (to earn or deserve).

senses.definition: To be the most successful in a game, competition, or race.

examples.text: Unsere Mannschaft möchte das Spiel gewinnen.
examples.translation: Our team wants to win the game.
examples.emotion: hopeful and determined, cheering on the team

senses.definition: To get something as a prize or reward in a lottery or contest.

examples.text: Er hat gestern im Lotto ein Auto gewonnen.
examples.translation: He won a car in the lottery yesterday.
examples.emotion: amazed and thrilled at sudden good fortune

senses.definition: To obtain or acquire something useful, such as time, information, or an advantage.

examples.text: Mit diesem Plan können wir wertvolle Zeit gewinnen.
examples.translation: With this plan we can gain valuable time.
examples.emotion: relieved and practical, seeing a clever solution

definitions: To be the most successful in a game, competition, or race.
To get something as a prize or reward in a lottery or contest.
To obtain or acquire something useful, such as time, information, or an advantage.
